action: Update Ivanti Endpoint Manager to 2024 SU8 or later now, starting with any Core server reachable from the internet, and review Core servers for signs of compromise.
exec: Endpoint Manager controls every managed computer; a no-login takeover flaw with public exploit code makes this a patch-now item.
plain: A serious weakness in Ivanti's software for managing company computers can let an outsider take control without a password. Instructions for abusing it are now public, so attacks are likely soon.

key_findings: CVE-2026-121653 is an SQL injection in the Core of Ivanti Endpoint Manager versions before 2024 SU8, rated CVSS 9.8.
A remote, unauthenticated attacker can inject SQL commands, which can lead to remote code execution.
Public proof-of-concept code for CVE-2026-121653 appeared by November 13, raising the chance of exploitation in the short term.
CVE-2026-18128 (CVSS 6.8): the Agent sends sensitive information in clear text, so a man-in-the-middle attacker can read and alter traffic.
recommendations: Install the updates Ivanti has released for Endpoint Manager.
See Ivanti's November 2026 security advisory for affected versions and fixes.

summary: The Dutch National Cyber Security Centre warns that proof-of-concept code is now public for CVE-2026-121653, an SQL injection flaw in the Core of Ivanti Endpoint Manager before 2024 SU8. A remote attacker without credentials can use it to run code. A second flaw, CVE-2026-18128, lets an attacker positioned on the network read and alter agent traffic sent in clear text. Ivanti has released updates.
title: NCSC Netherlands: public exploit code for critical Ivanti Endpoint Manager flaw (CVE-2026-121653)

validation.note: Reviewed against the original NCSC-NL advisory, read in a browser. The Ivanti advisory it references was not read.
